description:
## Goal

Make recursive structural meaning finite without constructing an ever-deeper concrete Ty ladder. Tuple and list nesting reproducers must terminate with bounded semantic work while preserving every runtime answer and every type distinction in the supported denotational domain.

The design has two phases. Phase 1 makes recursive equations canonical, interned regular-tree components without changing the public Ty / Types surface. Phase 2 makes each dynamic recursive activation component publish and close one coordinated system of return equations, then deletes the widening machinery that currently hides the ladder.

## Proven root problem

The immutable structural Ty language has no recursive-equation binder. Semantic construction eagerly embeds operand children, so T = :start | {int, T} expands inline forever. Activation-key count and return-widening budgets do not bound the cost: one activation can repeatedly construct deeper inputs.

Finite source syntax does not imply finitely many exact input classes. id(x) = x must remain parameterized rather than join unrelated callers. A recursive same_depth(a, b) can distinguish every nesting depth, so independent per-input finite partitions are unsound.

## Measuring stick: json_roundtrip product pull

The primary signal is a cold product-pull compile of fixtures2/behavior/json_roundtrip.fz through a real door, not Compiler2::drive() alone:

    fz2 --log-telemetry TRACE interp fixtures2/behavior/json_roundtrip.fz
    elixir tools/distill-telemetry.exs TRACE --top 20

Before each implementation phase, record a fresh baseline at the verified stack head. The distiller is authoritative for counts, not its span times: trace rendering inflates elapsed magnitudes on this fixture. Record job starts and re-runs, activation population, AnalyzeActivation runs, ReturnType revisions and widenings, causal wake sources, deliver_lanes and resume continuations, plus final backend canon. A plain-binary sample corroborates the time shape only.

The expected result is a massive collapse in causal work: no widening, finite recursive return types rather than fp[any] any, single-digit recursive return revisions and analyses, and material reductions in ladder-caused job, activation, wake, continuation, and shim counts. Fresh-baseline targets become lower-only test pins when implementation starts; no comparison may mix a standalone drive with a product-pull run. FIFO, LIFO, and permuted admission must retain identical semantic facts, artifact canon, output, and distilled causal shape.

## Phase 1 — canonical regular types and declared recursion

The closed kernel foundation (fz-kdt.177.4, .177.5, .177.11, and .177.6) owns the sole type-interner boundary for a regular component. A producer builds with local state references; that boundary canonicalizes and interns the component, returning one stable Ty per canonical state. The key is canonical component structure, never construction or allocation order. Ty remains opaque and compiler2 continues to use the existing Types operations.

Every former children-have-older-IDs argument must be replaced inside the kernel with the corresponding finite graph calculation: pair-memoized order, founded cycle-safe empty/subtype/equivalence traversal, guarded substitution and transforms, and mu-aware canonical rendering. No reference-count cycle, mutable descriptor identity, compatibility interner, inline unrolling, BDD copy, or second type authority is allowed.

fz-kdt.177.7 remains the narrow transport boundary: it proves a consumer that needs an exact root shape does not descend into a recursive component. fz-kdt.177.8 then resolves each typedef SCC atomically through the component boundary, publishes one TypeDefined fact per member, and removes self-waits. Self-recursive, mutually recursive, alpha-renamed, differently ordered, and finite-unrolled declarations must fold to the same identities. recursive_typedef becomes a three-door value fixture only when positive proofs replace the stalled diagnostic.

Retain the finite-type corpus and canonical-form census. Add direct regular-component tests for equality across unrollings, inequality of distinguishable cycles, construction-order-independent component bytes, repeated interning identity reuse, finite termination of every reader, and unchanged acyclic canonical identities.

Phase 1 exit: all three doors accept supported recursive typedefs and preserve runtime behavior; no consumer beyond Types, typedef resolution, and the narrow transport projection gains recursion-specific branching.

## Phase 2 — dynamic recursive return equations

fz-kdt.98.3 is the atomic prerequisite. It establishes the complete demand-rooted call-graph component and retained ComponentActivations inventory, then gives a recursive component one coordinated, derivation-owned ReturnType publisher. AnalyzeActivation remains the local-body authority; it must not independently publish member returns. A graph-only landing is forbidden because it exposes non-quiescing cyclic copies.

fz-kdt.177.10 closes the resulting regular equations through the Phase-1 component boundary. Internal return edges become local component edges; the solver reads only external ground evidence. An equation outside the supported regular algebra receives an explicit declared abstraction or diagnostic, never silent widening or structural erasure.

Once that solver owns the behavior, delete rather than bypass RETURN_WIDENING_BUDGET, ActivationSlot::ascents, return_type.widened, the define_return convergence/depth-cap path, their obsolete tests and telemetry claims, and the termination documentation they supported. Keep ReturnType and applied-event causality sufficient for the distiller; replace ladder pins with bounded component-publication pins.

Phase 2 exit: Json.value/1, Json.val/1, Json.decode/1, Json.array/2, and Json.array_element/2 publish finite recursive denotations and never widen. Internal cyclic copies do not re-wake member analyses; external callers wake only for a coordinated result. The fresh json_roundtrip telemetry pin proves that the work collapse comes from removing the recursive ladder, not from suppressing observation.

## Boundaries, deletion, and documentation

fz-kdt.177.12, .177.13, and .177.14 remain separate runtime-predicate work. They begin only if a recursive Ty reaches the general runtime predicate surface; they do not block the json_roundtrip return-ladder path.

Update set-theoretic-types, type-world, type-specialization, canonical-form, and performance-instrumentation with the final authority, supported equation algebra, telemetry baseline and result. Remove all temporary probes, old ladder pins, budgets, and obsolete termination claims in their owning tickets. Full focused, corpus, three-door, deterministic, formatting, check, and strict-Clippy gates must pass. One ticket means one commit and one close.

## Dependency order

- fz-kdt.177.7 → fz-kdt.177.8: supported declared recursion.
- fz-kdt.98.3 → fz-kdt.177.10: dynamic recursive returns and budget deletion.

Both paths depend on the already-tracked regular-component foundation and telemetry/reproducer pins (fz-kdt.177.1, .177.2, .177.3).

## UNBLOCKS

- ○ fz-kdt.64 P1 Retain exactly the supported semantic alternatives

## Historical aggravating case

On json_roundtrip at ac2543eb9, a product-pull trace recorded 4527 jobs, 54% re-runs, 380 activations for 140 functions, and 990 ReturnType-caused AnalyzeActivation wakes out of 1233. Json.value/1 revised its return 18 times and widened to any; twelve returns reached 15–18 revisions. Json.array_element/2 analyzed 77 times, Json.decode/1 55, Json.object_colon/3 32, and main/0 59. The erased returns then induced 315 deliver_lanes shims and 314 resume continuations. This establishes the mechanism and expected direction; every implementation comparison must first capture a fresh baseline at its verified stack head.

comments.text: LIST VARIANT of the same class (fz-kdt.183 cold review, 2026-09-03): `fn nest(acc, n), do: (if n == 0, do: acc, else: nest([acc], n - 1))` with nest([], 2) hangs (rc=124 at 40s) at 0889c0b3a for every n in {2,3,4,5,6,8}; the non-nesting control terminates in milliseconds. A self-nesting accumulator element -- tuple (this ticket) or list -- defeats the documented termination theorem in type-specialization.md:123-135 (no numeric singletons, finite atoms, return-join widening: none bounds element NESTING). Unaffected either way by 183's element-keyed prototype.

CONCORDANT with fz-kdt.65 (the RETURN_WIDENING_BUDGET side of the ladder): the budget counts strict ascents of the RETURN; a nesting accumulator ascends the INPUT key per rung with a super-linear Types cost per rung, so neither the return budget nor ACTIVATION_INPUT_ROW_BUDGET ends it in time. Note in .agent/docs/type-specialization.md:123-135 the termination carriers (no numeric singletons, finite atoms, return-join widening) do not name element nesting.

Measured (fz-kdt.177.2 review, json_roundtrip at 2d5f79d07): standalone semantic drive settles at 277 activations with a return revision / 843 analyses / max 9 revisions / 0 widened; the product pull every door takes reaches 380 activations / 1476 analyses / max 17 / 5 widened, and the three SHARED arrow-64 keys (Json.decode/1 9→17, val/1 8→17, value/1 8→17) climb the extra rungs. The pull's 103 extra activations are what feed the extra evidence into the shared returns: the ladder length is driven by the activation population, not by a demand edge on Json.value/1. Prediction for the kernel: a recursive denotation collapses the population and the ladder in one motion; the activation count (380 → ~126) and the revision count are one signal, not two.

title: Represent recursive denotations without expanding infinite type ladders
